header:
Date: 2025-09-11 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Asha Mehta (Nova - Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Nova - Infra Lead), Sara Chen (Nova - PM)
Recording: https://fireflies.example/recordings/ff-20250911-7892
summary: POC scoping focused on selecting an open-model shortlist for a multilingual fintech document processing POC. Discussed success criteria (accuracy on key info extraction, latency targets), workload sizing (1k doc sample, token distribution), benchmarks to run (quality + latency + cost matrix), timeline (data share by 9/15, benchmarks by 9/18, demo week of 9/22). Shortlist includes Llama 3 (commercial/open variants), Mistral 7B/Chat*, Falcon-40B-instruct, MPT-30B, and an instruction-tuned Vicuna-style variant; tradeoffs around latency, quantization friendliness, and multilingual quality were discussed. Security and deployment options covered (Hosted POC vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC); customer leans to start with Hosted POC but may require Dedicated if SLA/data residency needed.
topics: Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, do you all see the agenda I shared?
[00:06] Asha: Yep, thanks Maya, loud and clear. We want to get the POC scoped today - main goals are: extract key fields from loan docs and regulatory notices across English and French, eventual Spanish as a stretch.
[00:18] Diego: Cool, quick intro from me then we'll jump into success criteria and model choices. I'm Diego, SE on the inference side.
[00:25] Liam: Liam here, infra. We care about latency, cost, and also encryption at rest.
[00:30] Sara: Sara, PM, timeline is tight - legal review in mid October so we want results sooner.
[00:36] Maya: Great. First, success criteria - what would make the POC successful for Nova? Asha?
[00:42] Asha: Two things: quality and reliability. Quality is measured as 90% F1 on the labeled subset for key fields (borrower name, amount, term) and 95% extraction for regulatory flags. Latency, we'd like median < 400ms for single-turn extractions for a single-request path, throughput target is ~50 reqs/s for the pilot load. Cost is secondary but we want a ballpark token cost so we can compare hosted vs dedicated.
[01:08] Diego: Ok that's helpful. For 1k doc sample, do you have an average token count per doc?
[01:13] Asha: Average is about 2.3k tokens, distribution has a long tail - some legal notices go up to 8k.
[01:20] Diego: Noted. That affects model choice and KV cache planning. For the shortlist, we typically recommend a mix of smaller fast models and a larger higher-quality model. We're thinking open candidates: Llama 3 (instruct/chain variants), Mistral 7B Chat and Mistral-Instruct 7B, Falcon 40B-Instruct, MPT-30B-Instruct, and a tuned Vicuna/Vicuna-derivative that's instruction-finetuned.
[01:45] Sara: Quick question on Llama 3 — licensing? We need to confirm commercial usage for fintech.
[01:49] Maya: We'll attach the model licensing notes in the shared doc; initial assumption is some Llama variants are allowed for commercial but we'll confirm.
[01:56] Liam: Which of those are easiest to quantize? Our infra prefers int8 quantized footprints for Dedicated.
[02:02] Diego: Mistral and Falcon generally quantize well; Llama 3 has variants that are quantization-friendly but it depends on the binary/kernel support. MPT can be heavier. We'll include recommended quant profiles in the benchmark sheet.
[02:12] Asha: And multilingual quality - in our earlier tests we saw Mistral better on French compared to some others. Any data?
[02:19] Diego: Anecdotally yes; Mistral 7B Chat tends to handle Romance languages well. Falcon 40B has strong English and often good zero-shot for structured extraction but may need instruction-tuning for French. Llama 3's larger variants can be strong cross-lingually. We'll run the 1k-sample quality eval in EN/FR/ES to capture delta.
[02:36] Maya: Logistics - we'll start with Hosted POC so Redwood manages infra and we can iterate faster. If Nova needs data residency or an SLA, we can spin up Dedicated or Private for the next phase.
[02:46] Liam: For Hosted, what's the data retention? We need no retention by default and ability to bring-your-own-key.
[02:52] Maya: Standard hosted POC has configurable retention; we can disable retention and enable KMS for encryption in transit/at rest. We'll send security checklist.
[03:00] Sara: On benchmarks, what are the deliverables?
[03:03] Diego: Deliverables: 1) Quality matrix (F1/precision/recall per field per model per language), 2) Latency and throughput matrix (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens), 3) Recommendation and suggested production profile (quant, batch size, routing/pinning). We'll upload a shared spreadsheet and populate initial rows after you send sample.
[03:24] Asha: Sounds good. About the long-tail docs (8k tokens) — we worry about truncation and context window. Do we want retrieval-augmented or chunking?
[03:33] Diego: For long documents we recommend a chunk+retrieval approach for extraction; KV/prefix caching helps for repeated context. For final production, some models with larger context windows (or recent Llama 3 variants with extended context) could reduce complexity. For POC we'll simulate chunking and see quality impact.
[03:50] Liam: Cost question - if we run 1k docs across 5 models for EN/FR/ES, roughly what's the cost?
[03:57] Maya: We'll provide a cost estimate: hosted micro-billing for the benchmark run plus estimated per-token inference cost. Diego will include cost per 1k tokens per model in the sheet.
[04:06] Sara: Timeline recap?
[04:08] Maya: Customer to share 1k sample and labels by 2025-09-15. Redwood to run initial benchmark and share results by 2025-09-18. Follow-up demo to review results during week of 2025-09-22.
[04:19] Asha: That works. Also we need the security docs by 9/12 for our legal review.
[04:24] Maya: Affirmative, I'll send security checklist and licensing notes by EOD 9/12.
[04:28] Diego: Technical note — for consistent latency we'll test both single-threaded inference (low latency) and batched throughput. We'll report p50/p95/p99 and memory footprints.
[04:37] Liam: For Dedicated, what's the expected lead time if we decide after POC?
[04:41] Maya: Depends on capacity, but typically 4-6 weeks for Dedicated with reserved pools and networking, less if using an existing region. We'll include options.
[04:48] Sara: Any blockers we should be aware of?
[04:50] Asha: Licensing check for Llama variants and confirmation on encryption/retention.
[04:55] Diego: We'll add licensing notes and flag any models with commercial restrictions.
[04:58] Maya: Ok let's do a quick run through the model tradeoffs verbally:
[05:02] Diego: Mistral 7B: small, fast, good FR baseline, quantizes well, lower token cost but may need extra tuning for edge-case regulatory language.
[05:13] Diego: Falcon 40B-instruct: high-quality in English, strong extraction, slower, larger memory, good for higher-quality reference baseline.
[05:22] Diego: Llama 3 (mid/large): good cross-lingual, strong few-shot/instruction capability, variable licensing across variants — best for highest quality if allowed.
[05:32] Diego: MPT-30B: competitive but heavier and sometimes weaker on non-English unless specifically tuned.
[05:40] Maya: And tuned Vicuna-like variants could be a low-cost instr-tuned option but depends on the upstream base model.
[05:47] Asha: For the POC, do you recommend we pick 3 models or 5?
[05:51] Diego: Practically, 3 models gives a tight comparison (fast, mid, heavy). For completeness we can run 5 but focus analysis on 3. So our suggestion: Mistral 7B Chat (fast), Falcon 40B-Instruct (quality baseline), Llama 3 mid-sized (cross-lingual). Expand with MPT-30B and tuned Vicuna as extras if you want.
[06:14] Sara: That sounds reasonable. Any specifics on evaluation prompts?
[06:18] Diego: We'll use a mix: exact-match for structured fields, fuzzy-match for amounts and names, and human review for regulatory flag edge cases. We'll include evaluation code in the repo.
[06:28] Asha: Ok please make sure the human review is included in the plan — we need to sample edge cases.
[06:33] Maya: Noted. Last, can we confirm who owns what for next steps?
[06:36] Asha: I'll own dataset delivery.
[06:38] Liam: I'll review security checklist and confirm encryption options.
[06:41] Maya: Diego will run benchmarks. I'll send pricing and security docs.
[06:44] Sara: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[06:46] Maya: We'll recap in an email shortly with links to the shared spreadsheet and the timeline.
[06:50] Asha: Thanks, bye.
[06:52] End of recording

Notes: transcription contains small mis-hears (e.g., \"Mistral\" sometimes auto-corrected to \"Misteral\" in earlier runs), occasional crosstalk removed.
